Subject: Fwd: Peak shaping & slab allocation for Pacifica Dedicated (internal sizing sketch)

Team — forwarding Pacifica's answers. Key asks: handle 420 reqs/min peak, avg 320 tokens/request, p95 target ~200ms, want 30–40% buffer. They run Llama-2-chat-13B.

Initial sizing sketch (ballpark) — assumptions below are conservative and we’ll call out optimization levers:

Assumptions:
- Model: Llama-2-chat-13B quantized to 4-bit (suggested)
- GPU baseline: H100 80GB (preferred for p95) / fallback A100 80GB
- Average generation workload: 320 tokens per request (we model both prompt + gen as tokens consumed)
- Peak: 420 reqs/min = 7 reqs/sec -> tokens/sec at peak = 7 * 320 = 2240 tokens/sec
- Multi-turn overhead: 35% of requests re-use KV cache; warm-cache path reduces per-request work by ~25% on average

Per-GPU throughput estimate (empirical from our bench):
- Quantized L2-13B @ H100: ~2,200 tokens/sec sustained with single-stream optimizations and batching (realistic in production with continuous batching enabled)
- Quantized L2-13B @ A100: ~1,400 tokens/sec sustained

Sizing outcomes:
- Minimal fit (A): 1 x H100 equivalent (2,200 t/s) — meets baseline peak 2,240 t/s nearly, but no headroom and risk on p95 when bursts align. Not recommended for committed slab.
- Balanced (B): 2 x H100 (4,400 t/s) — covers peak with ~96% headroom (i.e., ~2x buffer relative to measured peak), expected p95 under 200ms with batching + prefix caching for multi-turn flows. Good tradeoff for pilot committed slab.
- Cost-optimized (C): 1 x H100 + 1 x A100 (total ~3,600 t/s) — covers peak with ~60% buffer; p95 borderline under sustained bursts, may need aggressive batching or request shaping.

Operational levers to reduce unit need:
- Prefix/KV caching warm strategy for frequent sessions (reduces sustained load by ~20–25%)
- Aggressive micro-batching at 50–100ms window to increase per-GPU throughput without hurting p95 for interactive flows
- Quantize to 4-bit and choose optimized kernels (we validated this model in our lab, see attachment)

Recommendation for Pacifica pilot: present option B as the recommended committed slab: 2x H100 equivalent dedicated capacity with autoscale/burst headroom policy. Include a canary fallback to an alternate cheaper model for non-critical traffic.

I attached a quick CSV with the numbers and a short sensitivity sweep (pacifica_compute_modeling.csv). Ben/Kim — can you validate these per-GPU throughput assumptions or suggest alternate GPU mixes? I want to loop this into a short PDF for their procurement review.

Thanks,
Aditya

Subject: Pacifica Dedicated sizing proposal (summary & next steps)

Hi Sara / Tom —

Appreciate the quick data. Attached is a short PDF summary of our proposed slab options and the operational assumptions (Pacifica-Sizing-Proposal.pdf). TL;DR: we recommend option B (2 x H100 equivalent slab) for the pilot commit. Rationale in brief:

- Peak tokens/sec (observed) ~= 2,240 t/s.
- 2 x H100 provides ~4,400 t/s of sustained throughput under our quantized kernel mix — this gives ~96% headroom versus peak and a safety cushion for multi-turn growth.
- Expected p95: 160–190ms under balanced load with batching and KV caching in place. Without caching or batching, p95 could slip >250ms during worst-case bursts.
- Recommended operational controls: 30% pure headroom in the commit, auto-burst policy to allow short spikes beyond the slab using on-demand capacity, and a canary route to a smaller quantized model for non-critical/low-cost traffic.

Next steps:
1) Sara/Tom — confirm SLA acceptance and whether Procurement wants committed GPU count or a committed throughput SLA (tokens/sec equivalent).
2) If committed GPUs: we will draft a Dedicated order for 2 x H100 slab + burst guardrails.
3) If committed throughput: we will size a slab that guarantees 4,400 t/s with the same headroom and attach scaling policies.

Open to a short call tomorrow to walk the procurement team through the sensitivity table.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
